beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A small square is one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rod is ten squares in a row: one ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three tens and four ones make thirty-four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The three counts the rods: three tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The four counts the loose squares: four ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two tens and no loose ones make twenty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The zero says there are no ones. Twenty is not two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count on by ones from fifty-seven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Fifty-eight.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Fifty-nine.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more. Now there are ten loose ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten ones join into one ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It slides over beside the other tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six tens, zero ones: sixty.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Sixty-one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Past one hundred, it works the same. One hundred eighteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One hundred nineteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more, and ten ones join into a ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It slides over: one hundred, two tens, zero ones. One hundred twenty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What number do these tens and ones show?

do.text: What number do these tens and ones show?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Five squares and one rod. I'll write fifty-one.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Wait. The rod is one ten. The tens digit goes on the left.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Five ones go on the right. That makes fifteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Tens on the left, ones on the right.
